transcript: Capt. Simon (phone): Major? That flash drive I got from the whistleblower is a real deal! I downloaded it into my laptop, and it contains thousands of important files!
Maj. Thorne (phone): Now, don't you lose that flash drive! It can't fall into wrong hands!
Capt. Simon (leaving, flash drive in hand, laptop left on the cafe table): I keep a close watch on it! I'm not an idiot!

fail_fact.title: You better protect your devices - all of them
text: Security disasters do not always start with a sophisticated attack. In 2000, an MI6 officer left a laptop containing classified training material in a taxi after drinking at a London tapas bar. The laptop was recovered, after MI6 placed an anonymous newspaper advertisement offering a reward.
In 2023, UK rail minister's government laptop was stolen from under his chair in a London pub, containing confidential information on strike negotiations. Luckily, it was remotely wiped.
The lesson is simple: protecting one secure device is pointless if you leave the rest of your workstation behind.
